text: Which of the following is the correct electron-dot (Lewis) structure of a nitrogen molecule (\(\text{N}_2\))? The four lettered structures (a)-(d) are shown in the figure.

options.label: A
options.text: Structure (a): two nitrogen atoms joined by a double bond (two shared electron pairs)

options.label: B
options.text: Structure (b): two nitrogen atoms joined by a single bond (one shared electron pair)

options.label: C
options.text: Structure (c): two nitrogen atoms joined by a triple bond (three shared electron pairs), with one lone pair on each \(\text{N}\) (i.e. \(\text{N} \equiv \text{N}\))

options.label: D
options.text: Structure (d): two nitrogen atoms joined by a single bond (one shared electron pair)

text: Which of the following structural formulae represents benzene? The four lettered structures (a)-(d) are shown in the figure.

options.label: A
options.text: Structure (a): a six-membered carbon ring with three alternating C=C double bonds and one H on each carbon (benzene, \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\))

options.label: B
options.text: Structure (b): a six-membered ring with two double bonds, some carbons bearing two H atoms

options.label: C
options.text: Structure (c): a six-membered carbon ring with all single bonds and two H on each carbon (cyclohexane, \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\))

options.label: D
options.text: Structure (d): a six-membered ring with two double bonds and one carbon bearing two H atoms
